hero.label: Made for HappyRobot
hero.headline: I want to help HappyRobot sell the AI brain logistics never knew it needed.
hero.subheadline: HappyRobot is doing something I find genuinely rare: building AI infrastructure for industries that actually move the world, not just the internet. The idea that freight brokers and carriers can run autonomous operations through an AI OS is the kind of leap that creates a new category, and I want to be on the team making those first calls. Pablo's vision of compounding intelligence for real-economy enterprises is exactly the kind of mission I want to grow inside of.

whyCompany.title: Logistics is a massive, underserved market finally ready for AI disruption
whyCompany.body: Supply chain and freight are trillion-dollar industries that have run on manual, repetitive phone calls and broker workflows for decades. HappyRobot is stepping into that gap at exactly the right moment, with purpose-built AI workers that understand the actual operational context. That is not a feature, that is a category-defining wedge.

whyCompany.title: YC-backed, early team, and the SDR role is a true ground-floor opportunity
whyCompany.body: HappyRobot is a YC S23 company actively scaling its sales motion, which means the SDR hired now will help define how the company goes to market, not just execute a playbook someone else wrote. That kind of ownership at 21 is rare, and I am not taking it lightly. Being early means the work I do now compounds into something much bigger.

whyCompany.title: My BDR experience selling AI to cold prospects maps directly to this role
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai, I ran cold outreach and LinkedIn sequences that helped the company land 15 to 20 paying clients, selling an AI product to decision-makers who were skeptical before they were convinced. That is exactly the motion HappyRobot needs: someone who can open conversations with logistics executives and make a complex AI value proposition feel urgent and real. I have done the reps, and I want to do them here.

quote: I spent over a year convincing skeptical buyers that AI could handle work they thought only humans could do, and now HappyRobot is proving that at an operational scale I did not think was possible this soon. I want to be the person making those first calls.
